# Review pack: review-api-design

Everything a worker needs for this skill, in one file: `SKILL.md`, `references/checklist.md`, the skill's other reference files and its language-neutral standards. Language-specific standards and signals are in `packs/review-api-design.<language>.md`. Where the instructions below say to load one of these files, use its section here instead; don't open the original. Citation columns (anchors, pages, source names) are left out: cite an element by its ID in `Finding.element` and the report script fills in `standard` and `url`. `sources.md` is maintainer material and is not included.

## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: API Design

Checks the OpenAPI/Swagger spec (existence, validity, match to implementation) and generic REST API design practice, using local, version-pinned summaries of the OpenAPI Specification and the Microsoft REST API Guidelines (Azure edition, plus the trace-context part of the Azure SDK guidance). Only the guidelines' generic HTTP/REST rules are used: rules that named an Azure-only mechanism were generalized or retired, so the checks apply to any HTTP API, whatever its language, framework or host. Severity comes from each element's own normative wording.

#### Inputs

`openapi.*`, `swagger.*`, controllers/routers, API DTOs, error-handling middleware, serializer/versioning config,
LRO/status-monitor endpoints, per `compliance-inventory`. If `compliance-inventory` found no API spec and no
controllers/routers, mark this whole subject N/A with a `notes` explanation — do not fabricate findings.

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/openapi-specification.md` — OAS-01…OAS-43. Load only when a spec file is in scope.
- `references/standards/azure-rest-api-guidelines.md` — AZ-001…AZ-110 (AZ-088, AZ-100, AZ-109 retired). Load when routes/controllers or a spec are in scope.
- `references/standards/azure-sdk-telemetry.md` — SDK-04, SDK-05 (SDK-01…SDK-03 retired). Load with the guidelines file.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill. Do not load `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation: apply the closest element if it clearly fits; otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md` and the standards files that apply (above).
2. If a spec exists, read its `openapi`/`swagger` value and apply only the OAS elements for that version (Ver column).
   Evaluate API-02 and API-03 with the OAS elements `checklist.md` lists for them, against the actual routes/DTOs.
3. If no spec exists but routes/controllers do, fail API-01 (raise an API-01 finding), mark API-02/API-03 N/A
   ("no spec"), and review the routes directly against the AZ and SDK elements.
4. For each check API-04…API-15, evaluate only the elements it lists whose "Applies when" condition holds in the
   files; if none apply, mark the check N/A with that reason (e.g. API-13 when no long-running operations exist).
   Every active element applies to every target, Azure-hosted or not. A `G†` element accepts any equivalent generic
   mechanism (header name, versioning style, error format); never fail a target for not using an Azure-specific name
   (`x-ms-*`, `api-version`, `azure-deprecating`) or format. Retired rows are not evaluated. Versioning is judged only
   under API-07.
5. Severity: each Finding takes the failed element's level — DO/DO NOT/MUST/MUST NOT/REQUIRED/SHALL → Error;
   (YOU) SHOULD/(YOU) SHOULD NOT/RECOMMENDED → Warning; (YOU) MAY/OPTIONAL → Information; REVIEW → the check's
   default. For a merged element with mixed levels, use the level of the part that failed.
   `checkResults.severityIfFailed` is always the check's default severity from `checklist.md`.
6. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `AZ-031`); the report script derives `standard` and `url`
   from it, so don't write them. For an OAS element, also set `page` to the spec's version line (`3.0.x`, `3.1.x`,
   `3.2.x` or `2.0`) so the link points at the matching specification page.
7. If neither a spec nor routes/controllers exist, return `checkResults` with every item `N/A` and
   `notes: "No API found in scope"`.
8. Boundaries: **owned here** — request-ID and `traceparent` headers documented in the contract (API-15); the
   throttling and overload response contract (`429`/`503`, `Retry-After`, retryability in error bodies); caching
   headers/ETags on HTTP APIs, pagination, the long-running-operation 202/status contract (API-13) and rate-limit
   responses; the Problem Details error format, method semantics and idempotency (AZ-009) and status-code choice,
   including 403 vs 404 (AZ-018); the API contract and its documentation (spec, versioning under API-07), including
   schema completeness in the spec (e.g. `additionalProperties`). **Don't fail for** whether a caller is authorized
   for a resource (review-security-identity-access SEC-IA-01/02; this skill judges only which status code is
   returned); runtime input validation and size limits (review-security-input-injection IV-06, IV-04);
   version-revealing headers, `405`/`415` handling, `Accept` reflection, credentials in request URLs and `no-store`
   on sensitive responses (review-security-web-api SEC-WA-07 … SEC-WA-10); request-ID/`traceparent` propagation and
   tracing in code (review-observability OBS-02/03); whether the service limits load (review-reliability AZRL-32)
   or honours `Retry-After` on outbound calls (AZRL-09); contract tests (review-testing TST-09); code-level design
   of controllers (review-software-quality).

#### Output

Findings, strengths and check results per `compliance-review-core`'s `finding-schema.md`.

## File: `references/standards/openapi-specification.md`

*Load rule: OAS-01…OAS-43. Load only when a spec file is in scope.*

### OpenAPI Specification — localized summary

- Ver column: `all` = same rule in 3.0/3.1/3.2; `differs` = the summary states the per-version rule; `2.0` = Swagger 2.0 only.
- Level `REVIEW` = locally derived review rule (spec ↔ implementation match); it takes the owning check's default severity.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Ver |
|---|---|---|---|
| OAS-01 | REQUIRED | Root `openapi` field holds the OAS version (`3.0.x`/`3.1.x`/`3.2.x`); select the rule set and citation base from it. `swagger: "2.0"` → OAS-43. | all |
| OAS-02 | REQUIRED | `info` with `title` and `version`; `info.version` is the API document's version, not the OAS version. | all |
| OAS-03 | REQUIRED / MUST | 3.0: `paths` is required. 3.1+: at least one of `paths`, `components`, `webhooks` MUST be present. | differs |
| OAS-04 | MUST / RECOMMENDED | Document is JSON or YAML; field names are case-sensitive; YAML map keys MUST be scalar strings; YAML 1.2 is RECOMMENDED. | all |
| OAS-05 | MUST | Fields not defined by the spec are invalid unless they are extensions starting with `x-`. 3.1+: `x-oai-`/`x-oas-` are reserved for the OpenAPI Initiative. | differs |
| OAS-06 | MUST | `components` map keys match `^[a-zA-Z0-9\.\-_]+$`. | all |
| OAS-07 | REQUIRED / MUST / SHOULD | Server URL variables are defined in `servers[].variables`, each with a `default`. `enum`: 3.0 SHOULD NOT be empty and default SHOULD be in it; 3.1+ MUST NOT be empty and default MUST be in it. | differs |
| OAS-08 | MUST | Every `paths` key begins with `/`. | all |
| OAS-09 | MUST NOT | Templated paths with the same hierarchy but different template names (e.g. `/pets/{id}` and `/pets/{name}`). | all |
| OAS-10 | MUST | Every `{template}` in a path corresponds to an `in: path` parameter at path-item and/or operation level (3.1+: except an empty path item). | all |
| OAS-11 | MUST / RECOMMENDED | `operationId` is unique across all operations (case-sensitive); RECOMMENDED to follow common programming naming conventions. | all |
| OAS-12 | MUST NOT | Duplicate parameters (same `name` + `in`) within one path-item or operation `parameters` list. | all |
| OAS-13 | REQUIRED | Each parameter has `name` and `in` ∈ `query`, `header`, `path`, `cookie`; 3.2 adds `querystring` (not combinable with `in: query` in the same operation). | differs |
| OAS-14 | REQUIRED / MUST | Path parameters declare `required: true`. | all |
| OAS-15 | MUST | A parameter has exactly one of `schema` or `content`; a parameter's `content` map has exactly one entry. | all |
| OAS-16 | SHALL | Header parameters named `Accept`, `Content-Type` or `Authorization` are ignored; describe them via `content`/security schemes instead. | all |
| OAS-17 | REQUIRED / SHALL / SHOULD | `requestBody.content` is required. Bodies on GET/HEAD/DELETE: 3.0 SHALL be ignored by consumers; 3.1 SHOULD be avoided; 3.2 SHOULD be avoided on GET/DELETE. | differs |
| OAS-18 | REQUIRED / SHOULD | 3.0: every operation has `responses`. 3.1+: optional, but a Responses Object has ≥ 1 code; if only one, it SHOULD be the success response. | differs |
| OAS-19 | REQUIRED | Response `description` is required in 3.0 and 3.1; optional in 3.2. | differs |
| OAS-20 | MUST | Status-code keys are strings (quoted in YAML); ranges use `1XX`–`5XX` (uppercase X); an explicit code overrides a range. | all |
| OAS-21 | MAY | `default` may describe all responses not declared individually (typically the error shape). | all |
| OAS-22 | REVIEW | `content` keys are media types or media-type ranges; for a request matching several keys only the most specific applies. | all |
| OAS-23 | MUST | Schema dialect: 3.0 = OAS subset of JSON Schema, nullability via `nullable`; 3.1+ = JSON Schema 2020-12, nullability via `type: [..., "null"]` (`nullable` is not a 3.1+ keyword). | differs |
| OAS-24 | REQUIRED | Every `$ref` resolves. 3.0: other keys beside `$ref` SHALL be ignored. 3.1+: a Reference Object allows only `summary`/`description` siblings. | differs |
| OAS-25 | REQUIRED / SHOULD / MUST | `discriminator.propertyName` is set and used with `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`. 3.0/3.1: the property SHOULD be required. 3.2: it may be optional, but then `defaultMapping` MUST be set. | differs |
| OAS-26 | SHOULD NOT | `readOnly` properties are not sent in requests; `writeOnly` properties are not sent in responses. | all |
| OAS-27 | REVIEW | `type`/`format` values (`int32`, `int64`, `float`, `double`, `date`, `date-time`, `uuid`, `byte`, `binary`, `password`) match the implementation's types. | all |
| OAS-28 | REVIEW | `required` arrays list exactly the properties the implementation always requires/returns. | all |
| OAS-29 | SHOULD | `example`/`examples` values match their schema. | all |
| OAS-30 | REVIEW | `enum` values in schemas match the implementation's enum values. | all |
| OAS-31 | REQUIRED | Each security scheme has a valid `type` (`apiKey`, `http`, `oauth2`, `openIdConnect`; `mutualTLS` 3.1+) with its required fields (`name`+`in`, `scheme`, `flows`, `openIdConnectUrl`). | differs |
| OAS-32 | MUST | Security requirement names match declared `securitySchemes`; scope list for oauth2/OIDC. Other types: 3.0 the array MUST be empty; 3.1+ it MAY list role names. | differs |
| OAS-33 | REVIEW | Root `security` applies by default and operation `security` overrides it; operations that are public in code use `security: []` (and only those). | all |
| OAS-34 | MUST | Tag names in the root `tags` list are unique. | all |
| OAS-35 | MUST | In Link Objects, `operationRef` and `operationId` are mutually exclusive and resolve to a real, unique operation. | all |
| OAS-36 | REVIEW | Operations/parameters/schemas that are deprecated in code carry `deprecated: true`, and vice versa. | all |
| OAS-37 | MUST | URL/email fields are well-formed (`termsOfService`, `contact.url`, `contact.email`, `license.url`). 3.1+: `license.identifier` and `license.url` are mutually exclusive. | differs |
| OAS-38 | REVIEW | Every implemented route + HTTP method appears in `paths`, and every documented path/method exists in code. | all |
| OAS-39 | REVIEW | Parameter names, locations (`in`), types and `required` match handler signatures and binding attributes. | all |
| OAS-40 | REVIEW | Request/response schemas match DTO property names (after the serializer naming policy), types, required-ness and nullability. | all |
| OAS-41 | REVIEW | Documented response status codes match the codes the handlers actually return (including error paths). | all |
| OAS-42 | REVIEW | Documented security matches the auth attributes/middleware applied to each route. | all |
| OAS-43 | MAY | Swagger 2.0 (`swagger: "2.0"`; `host`/`basePath`, `definitions`, `in: body`/`formData`, `consumes`/`produces`): check only the OAS-08 … OAS-14 equivalents and recommend migrating to OAS 3.x (Information). | 2.0 |

## File: `references/standards/azure-rest-api-guidelines.md`

*Load rule: AZ-001…AZ-110 (AZ-088, AZ-100, AZ-109 retired). Load when routes/controllers or a spec are in scope.*

### Microsoft Azure REST API Guidelines — localized summary

- Scope column: G = generic HTTP/REST practice, as the source states it. G† = generalized locally on 2026-11-12: the source rule names an Azure-only mechanism (`x-ms-*` headers, the `api-version` parameter, Azure error/deprecation headers, Azure host names), so the element keeps the source's intent and level but accepts any equivalent generic mechanism; the Azure form always satisfies it. Every active element applies to every target, Azure-hosted or not. No element requires an Azure-specific header, parameter, format or host.

#### URLs and idempotency

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-001 | DO | G | kebab-case (preferred) or camelCase URL path segments; camelCase when the segment names a JSON field. | routes |
| AZ-002 | DO | G | Service-defined path segments are case-sensitive; a case mismatch fails with 404. | routes |
| AZ-003 | DO | G | Service-defined path segments use only `0-9 A-Z a-z - . _ ~`; `:` only to mark an action. | routes |
| AZ-004 | YOU SHOULD | G | Restrict user-supplied path parameter values to the same set (no `:`). | path params |
| AZ-005 | YOU SHOULD | G | Keep URLs readable; avoid UUIDs and %-encoding where possible. | routes |
| AZ-006 | DO | G | Return 414 when a URL exceeds 2083 characters. | routes |
| AZ-007 | DO | G | URLs returned in headers/bodies use correct casing and one consistent form, regardless of the URL used to reach the resource. | URLs returned |
| AZ-008 | DO | G | Path shape `/<service-root>/<resource-collection>/<resource-id>`; collection names unabbreviated and plural; IDs are raw, URL-escaped values with no quoting. Host part: AZ-109. | routes |
| AZ-009 | DO | G | All HTTP methods are idempotent. | all ops |
| AZ-010 | YOU SHOULD | G | Create resources with PUT or PATCH. | create ops |
| AZ-011 | YOU MAY | G | POST may create, but must then be idempotent and return 201 with the created resource's URL. | POST create |

#### Status codes

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-012 | DO | G | Synchronous success codes: PATCH/PUT 200 or 201; POST-create 201 with the resource URL; POST-action 200; GET (item or list) 200; DELETE 204. | all ops |
| AZ-013 | DO | G | PUT/POST/DELETE that complete asynchronously return 202 and follow the LRO pattern. | LRO |
| AZ-014 | DO | G | Method names are case-sensitive and uppercase. | routes |
| AZ-015 | DO | G | PUT/PATCH/POST/GET return the resource state with 200/201. | resource ops |
| AZ-016 | DO | G | DELETE returns 204 with no body, even if the resource doesn't exist (no 404). | DELETE |
| AZ-017 | DO | G | Synchronous POST actions return 200 with a body (an empty object is allowed). | actions |
| AZ-018 | DO | G | 403 when access is denied, unless that leaks the resource's existence; then 404. | authz |
| AZ-019 | DO | G | Honor `If-Match`, `If-None-Match`, `If-Modified-Since`, `If-Unmodified-Since` (return ETag/last-modified); return a precondition-failed error if a precondition can't be verified. | resource ops |

#### Query parameters and headers

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-020 | DO | G | camelCase query parameter names. | query params |
| AZ-021 | DO | G | Validate every query parameter and request header value; fail with 400 and the standard error body. | params/headers |
| AZ-022 | DO | G | Parameter string formats: booleans `true`/`false`; integers within ±2^53−1; floats IEEE-754 binary64; UUID without braces; header dates IMF-fixdate; query date-time RFC 3339 (≤ 3 fractional digits); byte arrays base64; arrays comma-separated (preferred) or repeated `name=value`. | params |
| AZ-023 | DO | G† | Support the standard HTTP headers (`authorization`, `content-type`, `content-length`) and return a request ID (AZ-027) and, on errors, an error code (AZ-044). Azure's own header names (`x-ms-*`, `azure-deprecating`) aren't required. | headers |
| AZ-024 | DO | G | Header names are kebab-case. | custom headers |
| AZ-025 | DO | G | Compare header names case-insensitively; values case-sensitively when the header requires it. | headers |
| AZ-026 | DO | G | Accept HTTP-Date in headers and return IMF-fixdate (e.g. `Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT`). | date headers |
| AZ-027 | DO | G† | Generate an opaque value that uniquely identifies the request, return it to the caller (a response header with one consistent name, e.g. `request-id` or `x-request-id`; or a `traceId`/`requestId` field in every error body), and include it in error logs. | all ops |
| AZ-028 | DO NOT | G | Fail requests because of unrecognized headers (including distributed-tracing headers). | headers |
| AZ-029 | DO NOT | G | Use an `x-` prefix for new custom headers (RFC 6648), unless the header already exists in production. | custom headers |

#### REST resource design

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-030 | DO | G | Clear, consistent naming; resource paths that make sense; few required query parameters and JSON fields. | routes/DTOs |
| AZ-031 | DO | G | Response codes and bodies let callers diagnose and fix their own problems. | all ops |
| AZ-032 | DO | G | Define explicit string contracts (min/max length, legal characters, case sensitivity, standard formats). | string fields/params |
| AZ-033 | DO | G | One JSON schema per URL path for the PUT request/response, PATCH response, GET response and POST request/response; the PATCH request has the same fields with none required. | resource DTOs |
| AZ-034 | DO | G | Define each field's mutability (create / update / read-only); a passed read-only field fails unless it matches the current value. | resource DTOs |
| AZ-035 | DO | G | Keep fields simple and the hierarchy shallow. | DTOs |
| AZ-036 | DO | G | GET retrieves resources and returns JSON. | GET |
| AZ-037 | DO | G | Create/update with PATCH using JSON Merge Patch (`application/merge-patch+json`, RFC 7396). | PATCH |
| AZ-038 | DO | G | PUT with JSON for wholesale create/replace. | PUT |
| AZ-039 | DO | G | DELETE removes a resource. | delete ops |
| AZ-040 | DO | G | 400 with the standard error body for malformed requests or any JSON field name/value not understood by that version. | PUT/PATCH/POST |
| AZ-041 | DO NOT / YOU MAY | G | Never return secrets in GET responses; return them via POST only if absolutely necessary. | secret fields |
| AZ-042 | DO NOT | G | Add fields whose values are easily computed from other fields. | DTOs |
| AZ-043 | DO | G | PUT/PATCH processing: unknown/invalid or read-only field → 400; missing mandatory field → 400; create → 201; PATCH create-field mismatch on an existing resource → 409; update/replace → 200. | PUT/PATCH |

#### Errors

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-044 | DO | G† | Error responses carry a machine-readable string error code (body `error.code`, a Problem Details `type` URI or `code` extension); a dedicated header (e.g. `x-ms-error-code`) is optional. | error responses |
| AZ-045 | DO | G† | When an error-code header is also returned, its value equals the body's error code. | error responses with an error-code header |
| AZ-046 | DO / YOU MAY | G† | Error bodies use one consistent, documented shape: RFC 9457 Problem Details (`application/problem+json`: `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, `instance`, extensions allowed; e.g. ASP.NET Core `ProblemDetails`, Spring `ProblemDetail`) or the source's `{ "error": { "code"*, "message"*, "target", "details", "innererror" } }`; extra properties are allowed and outside the API contract. | error responses |
| AZ-047 | DO / YOU MAY | G | Unique, descriptive error codes for errors callers can recover from at runtime; common usage errors may share a few codes. | error codes |
| AZ-048 | DO / YOU MAY | G | Document top-level error codes as part of the API contract; they may be modelled as an extensible (model-as-string) enum. | error codes |
| AZ-049 | YOU SHOULD NOT | G | Add new top-level error codes without bumping the API version. | versioned APIs |
| AZ-050 | YOU SHOULD NOT | G | Document individual error status codes in OpenAPI when the `default` response describes them adequately. | OpenAPI spec |

#### JSON

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-051 | DO | G | camelCase JSON field names; acronyms not upper-cased. | DTOs |
| AZ-052 | DO | G | JSON field names and values are case-sensitive. | DTOs |
| AZ-053 | DO | G | Unique-ID values are opaque strings compared case-sensitively. | ID fields |
| AZ-054 | DO NOT | G | Send null-valued fields to clients; omit them instead. | responses |
| AZ-055 | DO | G | Accept null field values only in JSON Merge Patch requests (null = delete the field; 400 if it can't be deleted). | requests |
| AZ-056 | DO | G | Integers stay within the JSON-safe range (±2^53−1). | numeric fields |
| AZ-057 | DO | G | Well-known, parseable string formats; values round-trip across languages. | DTOs |
| AZ-058 | DO | G | Date-times are RFC 3339. | date fields |
| AZ-059 | DO / YOU MAY | G | Durations are fixed-unit numbers with the unit in the field name (`ttlSeconds`); RFC 3339/ISO 8601 intervals only when callers need calendar intervals. | duration fields |
| AZ-060 | DO | G | UUIDs follow RFC 4122. | UUID fields |
| AZ-061 | YOU SHOULD / YOU MAY | G | Prefer objects over arrays; arrays only when order matters; objects may group sub-fields. | DTOs |

#### Enums and polymorphism

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-062 | YOU SHOULD | G | Use extensible enums (string-modelled) unless the value set will never change. | enums |
| AZ-063 | DO | G | Document that new enum values may appear. | enums |
| AZ-064 | YOU SHOULD NOT / YOU MAY | G | Don't accept extensible-enum values not defined for the requested version; the service may return such values. | enums |
| AZ-065 | DO NOT | G | Remove enum values (breaking change). | enums |
| AZ-066 | DO | G | Polymorphic types have a discriminator field (e.g. `kind`) and carry the kind-specific fields in the body. | polymorphic DTOs |
| AZ-067 | YOU SHOULD / YOU SHOULD NOT | G | The discriminator is an extensible enum and cannot be changed by PATCH. | polymorphic DTOs |
| AZ-068 | YOU SHOULD NOT | G | Don't use arrays of polymorphic objects on updatable resources, or return polymorphic properties not defined for the requested version. | polymorphic DTOs |

#### Actions

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-069 | YOU SHOULD | G† | Actions use one consistent URL pattern that sets them apart from sub-resources (the source's `/<collection>/<id>:<action>` and `/<collection>:<action>`, or a verb sub-path such as `/<collection>/<id>/<action>`), with a verb as the action name. | actions |
| AZ-070 | DO | G | Actions use POST. | actions |
| AZ-071 | DO NOT | G | Use actions for behaviour expressible as standard Create/Read/Update/Delete/List operations. | actions |
| AZ-072 | DO / YOU SHOULD | G | Support `Repeatability-Request-ID` / `Repeatability-First-Sent` (OASIS Repeatable Requests) for POST that must be retry-safe. | non-idempotent POST |

#### Collections and query options

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-073 | DO / YOU SHOULD | G | List responses are an object with a top-level array, named `value` unless a better name exists. | list ops |
| AZ-074 | YOU SHOULD | G | Support server-driven paging whenever a collection could grow large. | list ops |
| AZ-075 | DO | G | `nextLink` is an absolute URL that includes every query parameter the service needs (incl. the version parameter, if the API uses one). | paged lists |
| AZ-076 | DO NOT | G | Return `nextLink` on the last page, or with a null value. | paged lists |
| AZ-077 | DO | G | Every list item includes `id` and `etag` (if supported; quotes escaped). | list ops |
| AZ-078 | DO | G | Document that items may be skipped or duplicated across pages. | paged lists |
| AZ-079 | YOU SHOULD NOT | G | Return a total `count` of the collection. | list ops |
| AZ-080 | YOU MAY / DO / DO NOT | G | May offer a GET list endpoint and `filter`, `orderby`, `skip`, `top`, `maxpagesize`, `select`, `expand` (and filter functions); these names are case-sensitive and not `$`-prefixed. | list ops |
| AZ-081 | DO | G | Return an error for an unsupported query parameter, filter operator or orderby field. | list ops |
| AZ-082 | DO | G | `skip`: integer, default and minimum 0. `top`: integer, minimum 1, default unlimited; returns up to `top` items starting at `skip`. `maxpagesize`: optional integer with a default, documented as possibly returning fewer items. | query options |
| AZ-083 | DO | G | Apply query options in the documented order, with `select`/`expand` last; keep the same filter and sort across all pages. | query options |
| AZ-084 | DO | G | Filter/sort semantics: drop items where the filter is false, null or references properties hidden by permissions; ascending by default; nulls sort first; use the type's natural order; standard operator precedence; ties broken by the next expression. | filter/orderby |

#### Versioning and deprecation

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-085 | DO | G† | Every operation is versioned explicitly through one consistent mechanism: a query parameter (e.g. `api-version`), a request header, a media-type parameter or a path segment. | all ops |
| AZ-086 | DO / DO NOT | G† | Version values follow one documented scheme (e.g. date-based `YYYY-MM-DD` with `-preview`, or major/semantic versions); a new version never reuses the value of an earlier or preview version. | versions |
| AZ-087 | DO | G† | A missing (when required) or unsupported version returns 400 with the standard error body and a descriptive error code (Azure: `MissingApiVersionParameter` / `UnsupportedApiVersionValue`). | all ops |
| AZ-089 | DO NOT | G | Make breaking changes within an existing API version. | versioned APIs |
| AZ-090 | DO | G† | Announce a removal only when the operation will stop working and the client must act, in a machine-readable form: `Deprecation` (RFC 9745) and `Sunset` (RFC 8594) headers with a `Link` to details, or one documented equivalent (Azure: `azure-deprecating`). | deprecations |

#### Long-running operations

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-091 | DO / DO NOT | G | Use an LRO when p99 latency is over 1 s; never make PATCH an LRO; never use a long-running POST to create (use PUT). | slow ops |
| AZ-092 | DO | G | Validate as much as practical synchronously before starting an LRO. | LRO |
| AZ-093 | DO / YOU SHOULD / YOU SHOULD NOT | G | Every LRO initiation returns an absolute `operation-location` header to the status monitor (SHOULD carry the request's version parameter, if any). DELETE and POST-action LROs return 202 and no other 2xx, even if already complete. PUT-based patterns: AZ-102, AZ-105. | LRO |
| AZ-094 | DO | G | Accept a client `Operation-Id` header, generate an ID (typically a GUID) if absent, return it in `Operation-Id`, and answer 409 on reuse unless the request is an identical retry. | LRO |
| AZ-095 | DO / DO NOT | G | Status monitor body: `id`, `status` ∈ NotStarted/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Canceled, `error` on failure, `result` only for action LROs (never for resource LROs), `kind` when polymorphic, plus any values needed to form the GET; POST-action LROs return it in the body. | LRO |
| AZ-096 | DO | G | GET on the status monitor returns 200, includes an integer-seconds `retry-after` until terminal, and the monitor is kept for a publicly documented period (≥ 24 h) after completion. | LRO |

#### Conditional requests and telemetry

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-097 | YOU SHOULD | G | Return an `ETag` from any operation that returns or updates a resource. | resource ops |
| AZ-098 | DO | G | Conditional behaviour: GET `If-None-Match` match → 304; PUT/PATCH `If-None-Match: *` with an existing resource → 412; `If-Match` mismatch → 412; DELETE `If-Match` match → 204, mismatch → 412. | conditional headers |
| AZ-099 | YOU SHOULD / DO | G | ETag is a hash of the whole representation (strong if range requests are supported) and differs per content encoding. | ETags |

#### Long-running operation patterns

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-101 | DO | G | LRO initiation responses include any extra headers needed to build the GET poll request (e.g. `location`). | LRO |
| AZ-102 | DO / YOU SHOULD | G | Create-or-replace with long-running processing: `PUT` (optional `operation-id` header) returns 201 (create) or 200 (replace), not 202; body = the resource, same schema as the request; `Operation-Id` header; SHOULD add absolute `Operation-Location` with the request's version parameter, if any. Idempotent retry → same response; non-idempotent repeat → overwrite or 409. | PUT LRO |
| AZ-103 | DO | G | DELETE LRO: `DELETE` (optional `operation-id`) returns 202 with `operation-id` and `operation-location`; 400 if a request body is sent. | DELETE LRO |
| AZ-104 | DO | G | LRO action on an existing resource: `POST <resource>:<action>` (optional `operation-id`) returns 202 with `operation-id`, `operation-location` and a status-monitor body; an idempotent retry returns the same response. | POST-action LRO |
| AZ-105 | DO / YOU SHOULD | G | LRO action with no related resource (e.g. batch): `PUT <operation-endpoint>/<operation-id>`; operation ID required as the final path segment; SHOULD use one endpoint per action; returns 201 with `operation-location` and a status monitor holding status, request parameters and the eventual result or error; SHOULD serve the monitor from GET on the same URL and use it as `operation-location`. | resource-less LRO |
| AZ-106 | DO / YOU SHOULD | G | Polling: `GET <operation-endpoint>/<operation-id>` returns 200 with the status monitor (plus `retry-after` while not terminal) and SHOULD accept any supported API version, not only the one used to start the operation. | LRO |
| AZ-107 | YOU MAY / YOU SHOULD | G | Status-monitor collections: MAY support a GET list; SHOULD support listing for resource-less LRO actions; SHOULD support `filter` on `kind` for polymorphic monitor collections. | LRO |

#### Substrings, service host and correlation

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZ-108 | DO | G† | Every string offset or length in a response states its unit (UTF-8 bytes, UTF-16 code units or code points) by field name, schema or documentation; the source's `{ "utf8", "utf16", "codePoint" }` object satisfies this. | responses with text offsets/lengths |
| AZ-110 | MUST / SHOULD | G† | A client-supplied request ID header (e.g. `client-request-id`; Azure: `x-ms-client-request-id`), when accepted, is logged and not assumed unique; the service-generated request ID (AZ-027) is globally unique (MUST) and SHOULD be logged with traces. | all ops |

## File: `references/standards/azure-sdk-telemetry.md`

*Load rule: SDK-04, SDK-05 (SDK-01…SDK-03 retired). Load with the guidelines file.*

### Azure SDK general guidelines (telemetry and distributed tracing) — localized summary

- The source is written for **client libraries**; each element restates a client rule as what the **service** must accept, propagate or capture. Only its generic trace-context rules are kept: the Azure SDK `User-Agent` format and the `x-ms-*` telemetry headers (SDK-01 … SDK-03) were retired on 2026-11-12 because they apply only to Azure SDK callers. G† = generalized locally (see `azure-rest-api-guidelines.md`). Level keeps the client rule's rendered wording (DO / YOU SHOULD), which sets the severity.

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement for the service (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SDK-04 | DO | G | Accept W3C Trace Context headers (`traceparent`, `tracestate`) and continue the caller's trace, using the incoming context as the parent span. | all ops |
| SDK-05 | DO | G† | Instrument request handling with OpenTelemetry and populate span attributes per the OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions (the source names the Azure tracing conventions, which build on them). | all ops |
